question: Does one trained official selective SSM give the same outputs when the same test trajectory is (a) fed on its native observation grid with physical step sizes and (b) resampled onto the training grid, and what does each cost in task loss and inference time?

implementation_fixed_before_results.name: TIDES (official PyTorch)
implementation_fixed_before_results.entry_point: tides.TIDES(d_input, d_hidden, ssm_size, ssm_blocks, num_blocks, ...).forward(x, step_scale)
code_facts_verified_by_reading: step = step_scale * exp(log_step): step size proportional to the physical gap (per-mode timescale)
scan x_k = Lambda_bar_k x_{k-1} + B_bar_k u_k with step_scale_from_indices giving the gap before k (right-endpoint convention in code; paper Eq. 2 is written left-endpoint)
optional causal conv1d over tokens (conv_kernel_size, default 0)
BatchNorm1d(affine=False) over batch and time per channel before each SSM
TIDESClassifier pools by h.mean(dim=1), a sample-count mean
pure-PyTorch associative scan; scripts fall back to CPU when CUDA is absent
selection_criteria: runs on CPU without custom CUDA/Triton kernels
per-step physical step sizes supported natively, so native-grid evaluation needs no model change

task.name: CT-teacher regression (one small synthetic task)
task.teacher: FIRST_RUN continuous-time selective toy with the parameters of FIRST_RUN unit 0 (fixed)
task.inputs: sine-sum path per trajectory, seed = 1_000_000 + trajectory_id (disjoint from all earlier seeds)
task.labels: teacher output y(t) on the continuous path at the training-grid times t_k = k*T/K (physical query times; identical across all test conditions)
task.normalization: input and label mean/std from the TRAIN split on the training grid; reused unchanged for every grid and mode

split.order: split trajectory IDs FIRST, then build grids per split

task.label_reference: scssm.reference.ct_true with 128 RK4 sub-steps per training interval

test_conditions.S2/S4/S8: PRIMARY refinement: every interval split into m sub-steps with the held value repeated (same held path)
test_conditions.H8: PRIMARY refinement with a density change: only first-half intervals split into 8 (same held path)
test_conditions.J1: SECONDARY, not a refinement: random observation times (K observations, rng seed 2_000_000 + trajectory_id); the held path differs by construction

modes.native: feed the condition's grid with step_scale = dt_k / dt_train; read outputs at training times (for J: last output at or before each training time)
modes.resampled_locf: PRIMARY simplest alternative: last observation carried forward onto the training grid (causal), step_scale = 1
modes.resampled_linear: SECONDARY: linear interpolation onto the training grid (NON-causal, uses the next observation); labelled as such

training.note: single fixed setting, no sweep; dev (calibration) split used only for checkpoint selection (R-A1)

metrics.discrepancy: rel_l2 over the 33 training-grid times between a condition's output and native C0 output, per test trajectory
metrics.task_loss: MSE to the teacher labels at training-grid times, original units, per test trajectory
metrics.inference_cost: median of 3 wall-clock timings per condition batch on 2 CPU threads, and tokens processed (sequence length)
metrics.aggregation: mean over the 256 test trajectories with a 95% percentile bootstrap CI (2000 resamples, seed 0); paired native-minus-resampled differences per trajectory
metrics.equivalence_rule: Say 'no practical difference' only if the 95% CI of the paired MSE difference lies inside +-5% of the resampled_locf mean MSE; otherwise report the direction or 'inconclusive'. A non-significant difference is NOT equivalence.
metrics.float32_floor: differences below 1e-4 relative are treated as numerically indistinguishable (FR-E4-N4 emulation)

predictions_before_results.R-P1: native split discrepancy at S8 exceeds the float32 floor, because block 2 receives extra internal samples of block 1's output (P1-COMP-01 mechanism)
predictions_before_results.R-P2: resampled_locf split discrepancy at S2/S4/S8 is exactly 0 up to float32, by construction (S grids contain the training times)
predictions_before_results.R-P3: DROPPED by amendment R-A2 (N conditions removed)
predictions_before_results.R-P4: native inference cost grows with the number of tokens; resampled cost is constant in m
predictions_before_results.R-P5: on H8, |native sample-mean pooled change vs C0| > |time-weighted pooled change vs C0| (paired bootstrap CI of the difference excludes 0)

amendments.status: PRE_RUN (adapter check and timing smoke used 4 TRAIN trajectories and untrained weights only)
amendments.change: Checkpoint selection on the calibration (dev) split: dev MSE (original units, training grid) is evaluated every 100 steps; the state with the lowest dev MSE (earliest on ties) is saved, hashed (sha256) and frozen BEFORE any test trajectory is generated or evaluated. Replaces 'dev used only to report dev loss'.
amendments.reason: requested; avoids choosing the checkpoint on test data

amendments.change: Refinement conditions are restricted to the SAME held path: S2/S4/S8 (all intervals split, held value repeated) and H8 (only first-half intervals split by 8, a density change). N2/N4/N8 (new observations) are removed because they change the held path. J1 (random observation times, K observations) is kept as a SECONDARY non-refinement condition; J0.5 and J2 are dropped.
amendments.reason: requested: refinement must keep the same held path

amendments.change: The resampler receives only the test grid (observation times and observed values); it has no access to the continuous path. LOCF outputs are therefore always observed values (unit test). The continuous path is used only to compute labels.
amendments.reason: requested: no unobserved high-resolution truth in the resampler

amendments.change: Add a pooled readout and a pooling-only ablation. Pooled label: exact time average (1/T) int_0^T y_true dt of the teacher on the continuous path (Simpson on the RK4 nodes). Arms on the SAME checkpoint and test trajectories: native (per-step outputs; pooled = sample mean over all native tokens, as TIDESClassifier's h.mean(dim=1) with a linear head), resampled_locf (training grid; pooled = sample mean over training tokens), pooling_only (identical native per-step outputs; pooled = right-endpoint time-weighted sum over native tokens). Because the head is linear, pooling predictions equals pooling hidden states then applying the head.

Equivalence margin made explicit. Unit: the per-trajectory test MSE in original label units. Margin: delta = 0.05 x mean_i MSE_resampled,i (the resampled_locf arm, same condition), applied to the mean paired difference mean_i (MSE_native,i - MSE_resampled,i). 'No practical difference' only if the 95% percentile bootstrap CI (2000 resamples of test trajectories, seed 0) lies inside (-delta, +delta); 'native better/worse' if the CI excludes 0 on one side; otherwise 'inconclusive'. Rationale: a convention fixed before any trained-model result; +-5% in MSE is about +-2.5% in RMSE; it is not derived from any application cost, and all CIs are reported so other margins can be applied. A non-significant difference is never read as equivalence. Discrepancies below 1e-4 (emulated float32 floor, FR-E4-N4) are treated as numerically indistinguishable.
Seed 0 is the only training seed: results are a CONDITIONAL PILOT for this seed and initialization, not evidence about the training algorithm's performance distribution.

Training cap: 900 s wall clock for the training stage (timing smoke: about 0.03 s per batch-32 step, projected about 66 s for 2000 steps; label generation in pure Python adds about 2-3 min). Evaluation cap: 900 s. Seeds: python random, numpy and torch set to 0 before building the model (TIDES initialization also draws from numpy's global RNG).

Added directional prediction R-P5 (from FR-E3): on H8, the change of the native sample-mean pooled readout relative to C0 exceeds that of the time-weighted pooled readout; evaluated by the paired bootstrap CI of |dmean| - |dtime| (per trajectory). R-P3 is dropped with the N conditions.

Per-step readout at base times for J1 (native): last native output at or before each base time (uses model outputs only). Runtime: median of 3 wall-clock timings of one batch containing all 256 test sequences per condition and arm, 2 CPU threads, float32.
